# Error codes

Every Substrat surface answers a refusal as an [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) problem document, served as `application/problem+json`. The `code` it carries comes from one closed list, the same on every surface: a module never invents a code, it narrows one with a `reason` of its own. Each code has a page here, and the page's address is the `type` the document carries, so a refusal links to its own explanation.

```json
{
  "type": "https://substrat.net/errors/permission-denied",
  "title": "Permission denied",
  "status": 403,
  "detail": "permission denied: customer:manage",
  "instance": "/api/op/customer/update",
  "error": "permission denied: customer:manage",
  "code": "permission_denied",
  "permission": "customer:manage"
}
```

## The codes

| `code` | Status | Title | Means |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`unauthenticated`](/errors/unauthenticated) | `401` | Unauthenticated | The request carried no credential this surface accepts. |
| [`permission_denied`](/errors/permission-denied) | `403` | Permission denied | A permission check refused a caller the surface knows. |
| [`forbidden`](/errors/forbidden) | `403` | Forbidden | A policy refused the request, whatever the caller's permissions. |
| [`not_found`](/errors/not-found) | `404` | Not found | The addressed thing does not exist, or does not exist for this caller. |
| [`conflict`](/errors/conflict) | `409` | Conflict | The request is well formed, but the current state does not allow it. |
| [`validation_failed`](/errors/validation-failed) | `400` | Validation failed | The input did not parse, or broke a rule about its own values. |
| [`precondition_failed`](/errors/precondition-failed) | `412` | Precondition failed | A precondition the caller sent no longer holds. |
| [`rate_limited`](/errors/rate-limited) | `429` | Rate limited | The caller is over a request budget. |
| [`unavailable`](/errors/unavailable) | `503` | Service unavailable | A fact about the deployment, not the request, stopped the answer. |
| [`internal`](/errors/internal) | `500` | Internal error | The platform failed, and the reason is not sent. |

Switch on `code`, never on the status or the sentence. Two codes share `403`, and `detail` is written for people.

## The body

The members a problem may carry. A member with codes beside it appears only on those codes; the rest may appear on any problem.

- `type`: The canonical identifier: `https://substrat.net/errors/<code>`, the page for that code. `about:blank` when the body names no code.
- `title`: Short and human, and the same for every occurrence of a code. Do not parse it.
- `status`: The HTTP status, repeated from the status line (RFC 9457 §3.1.2).
- `detail`: What went wrong this time, as a sentence for a person. Never present on `internal`.
- `instance`: The path of the request this answers, when the surface knows it.
- `error`: A deprecated copy of `detail`, kept while older clients still read it. Read `detail`.
- `code`: The taxonomy entry, one of the codes on this page. The member to `switch` on. Absent exactly when `type` is `about:blank`.
- `requestId`: The id of the request that failed, the same as its `x-substrat-request-id` header. Quote it when reporting a failure.
- `permission` ([`permission_denied`](/errors/permission-denied)): The permission key the check refused.
- `entity` ([`permission_denied`](/errors/permission-denied), [`precondition_failed`](/errors/precondition-failed)): The record the refusal is about, as an entity reference (`{ entityType, entityId }`).
- `reason` ([`forbidden`](/errors/forbidden), [`not_found`](/errors/not-found), [`conflict`](/errors/conflict), [`validation_failed`](/errors/validation-failed), [`precondition_failed`](/errors/precondition-failed), [`unavailable`](/errors/unavailable)): A slug the refusing module owns, narrowing the code: snake_case, at most 64 characters. Branch on it; never show it.
- `errors` ([`validation_failed`](/errors/validation-failed)): One entry per field that failed to parse: `path`, dotted into the input, and `message`.
- `retryAfter` ([`rate_limited`](/errors/rate-limited)): Seconds to wait before retrying, the same value as the `Retry-After` header.
- `storeCode` (any code): The scope store's own error code, when the refusal came from a store. It is the store's vocabulary, not this taxonomy's.
- `storeBody` (any code): The scope store's own error body: only a refusal's (a `4xx`), and only up to 1024 bytes of JSON.

## A body with no `code`

When a surface has a status and nothing else, the body is RFC 9457's `about:blank` form. That happens when it relays a refusal raised somewhere else, or answers a throw nobody typed. The `title` is the status phrase and `code` is absent:

```json
{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Bad request",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "the shop is closed on Sundays",
  "instance": "/api/op/shop/checkout",
  "error": "the shop is closed on Sundays"
}
```

The absence is the answer, not an omission. A client switching on `code` falls through to its default branch instead of matching a code that would be a guess. Handle it by the status, and show `detail`.

## Where this comes from

The codes, statuses, titles and members on these pages are read from `@substrat-run/contracts` (`errors.ts`), the same registry every surface renders its problems from, and CI fails if a page falls behind it. [What a good API looks like](/concepts/api-design#_5-failures-are-data) explains why failures are part of the surface.
